name: BMW M4 (F82)
reliability: 7/10 — the F82 M4 is fast, tunable, and lighter than it looks (carbon roof and driveshaft), but the S55 twin-turbo six carries the headline modern-M concern: single-bolt crank-hub slippage, which can throw off timing and cause misfire/failure — overwhelmingly on tuned or hard-launched cars, but it defines the platform's reputation. Beyond that it's a factory plastic charge pipe that cracks, intercooler (charge-air cooler) failures, and the usual water-pump/thermostat wear. A stock or lightly-tuned car with the crank hub addressed is a strong, thrilling coupe; abused, tuned cars are the ones to scrutinize.
cost_to_own: Insurance: High · Maintenance ~$1,000/yr, more if you tune (crank hub, cooling) · Depreciation has flattened; clean manuals hold value best
popular_mods: A crank-hub upgrade (pinned/keyed) — the essential first step before any serious S55 power
An aluminum charge pipe to replace the crack-prone factory plastic one
A tune plus an upgraded intercooler — the S55 makes big, safe gains with cooling support
Coilovers or springs to calm the firm, occasionally twitchy stock chassis
Honest take: if you tune it, do the crank hub and cooling first — that's what keeps a big-power S55 alive
oil_type: BMW LL-01 synthetic (0W-30 / 5W-40 — the S55 does NOT use the 10W-60 of older M engines)
oil_interval: Every 5,000–7,500 miles (short of BMW's condition-based interval)

generations.M4 (2015–2020, F82): The coupe half of the F80 M3 / F82 M4 pair and the first M3/M4 to trade a naturally-aspirated V8 for a twin-turbo six — a huge torque and efficiency gain, with carbon-fiber weight savings. Quick and endlessly tunable, if firmer and less delicate than the smaller M2.
generations.Competition Package (2016+): Bumped output to ~444 hp with retuned suspension, wheels, and a sportier exhaust — the more sorted way to buy an F82.

common_issues: Single-bolt crank-hub slippage — the marquee S55 concern (mostly tuned/launch-control cars), can cause timing/misfire failure
Factory plastic charge pipe cracking under boost
Oil-consumption and rod-bearing debate on hard-driven cars
Water-pump and thermostat wear with age
maintenance_tips: Address the crank hub before any meaningful tune or repeated hard launches
Replace the plastic charge pipe with aluminum proactively
Use the correct LL-01 low-viscosity synthetic — not the 10W-60 that older M engines require
Support any tune with an upgraded intercooler and healthy cooling system
Service the DCT fluid on schedule and monitor clutch adaptations on DCT cars

engine.detail: 3.0L S55B30 twin-turbo inline-six — 425 hp (444 hp Competition), 406 lb-ft from just 1,850 rpm via twin mono-scroll turbos on an open-deck block. The first turbo M4.
engine.watch: The marquee concern is single-bolt crank-hub slippage — it can throw off timing and cause misfire or failure, overwhelmingly on tuned or hard-launched cars; pin/key the hub before serious power. The factory plastic charge pipe cracks under boost (aluminum is the fix) and the charge-air intercooler can fail; oil consumption and the rod-bearing debate follow hard-driven cars, and the water pump/thermostat wear with age. Use LL-01 low-viscosity synthetic — never the 10W-60 of older M engines.

drivetrain.detail: Rear-wheel drive through a 7-speed M-DCT dual-clutch or a 6-speed manual, with a carbon-fiber driveshaft and an active M differential.
drivetrain.watch: Service the DCT fluid on schedule and monitor clutch adaptations on DCT cars; the manual is durable and the value-holding choice.

suspension.detail: Adaptive M suspension with a double-joint aluminum front and five-link rear — firmer and occasionally twitchy at the limit.
suspension.watch: The stock chassis can feel nervous near the edge — coilovers or springs calm it; refresh bushings on older cars.

brakes.detail: M compound vented discs with blue four-piston front calipers; carbon-ceramics optional.
brakes.watch: Pads and fresh fluid are all track use needs; the optional ceramics are expensive to service.

body.detail: Steel unibody coupe lightened with a carbon-fiber roof and driveshaft — lighter than it looks at ~3,530 lbs.
body.watch: Mostly rock chips and the usual coupe seal wear; rust is uncommon.
